sources.note: Formalizes test-time scaling as budgeted inference over a model's implicit prefix tree, separates three structurally different regimes that a single scalar budget conflates, specifies what a reproducible inference protocol must declare, and releases 1.9 million traces — with the empirical section showing a selection score that makes accuracy fall from 75.56% to 65.83% as the candidate bank grows.
sources.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility

sources.note: Spends test-time compute on iteratively refining each sampled rollout rather than on drawing more of them, then majority-votes the refined answers, with no verifier.
sources.title: Refining Over Resampling: Test-Time Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Reformulates test-time reasoning as compute allocation over partial trajectories under a hardware budget, and runs a zero-sum beam search over reasoning steps that prunes weak traces and immediately re-spends the freed capacity by branching from high-scoring prefixes.
sources.title: Thought-Level Beam Search for Reasoning

sources.note: Shows that which layers a steering vector should be injected at is a property of the individual input rather than of the task, that a greedy per-input rule reaches the exhaustive optimum for structural reasons, and that a label-free predictor trained to imitate that rule recovers most of the oracle at deployment.
sources.title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models

sources.note: Replaces uniform test-time compute allocation with a training-free agent that picks reasoning tools, a search strategy and an exploration parameter per problem, using a process reward model both to prune within a trajectory and to select across iterations.
sources.title: What If We Allocate Test-Time Compute Adaptively?

result.definition: Keeping a fixed number of partial candidates and extending the best of them, and across 5 sources the search baseline in test-time-scaling comparisons -- generally beaten by methods that reduce completed candidates rather than search over unfinished ones. Its distinctive property in the archive's taxonomy is that it operates on partial states, which is a different statistical object from sampling completed candidates and reducing them, and one source's argument is that reporting these under one scalar budget makes results incomparable. Where it is adapted rather than used as a baseline, the adaptation is about what the freed capacity does: a thought-level variant treats pruning as zero-sum, immediately re-spending the capacity released by dropping a weak trace on branching from a high-scoring prefix, which is what makes prefix caching load-bearing for it.
